mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and independent of other series.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5%, it indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days. The interaction effect is stronger than either series alone.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 1900.0 and INDPRO > 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 200), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.0% triggers monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 200 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: A positive trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days. The signal is always active and independent of other series.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in high HOUST periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceed 130,000.0 (thousand persons), it signals robust job growth that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS > 130000.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery regime (HOUST > 2000.0 and RSAFS > 350000.0), rising housing starts and strong retail sales indicate a consumer spending boom that produces positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 2000.0 and RSAFS > 350000.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% and fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% indicates tight monetary policy during a strong labor market, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to reduced corporate investment.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy during strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5 and UNRATE < 5.0.
